work.permit: Minor's Employment Certificate (Guam Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division)

note: Read in the Guam Code Annotated as the Compiler of Laws publishes it (col.guamcourts.gov). Majority: 18, 19 GCA § 1101: minors are all persons under eighteen. Emancipation by marriage or court declaration isn't held. Work: 14. 19 GCA ch. 11 (Child Labor Law): no minor under sixteen may work until the employer keeps an employment certificate issued by the Wage and Hour Commissioner (§ 11104); minors of 14 and 15 may work outside school hours within limits (§ 11106(b)); the Guam Department of Labor's handbook (16 February 2026) says the certificate is required only for 14 and 15 year olds. Guam's law sets no age below 14 in words; the federal Fair Labor Standards Act, which the handbook says also binds employers, does, and 14 is the age both meet. Newspaper delivery from 12 and work for parents aren't held. Performers: permit, the reading being that § 11104's certificate covers every minor under 16 and § 11108(c) lets the Commissioner set by regulation the conditions on which those under sixteen may work as dancers, singers, musicians, entertainers, motion picture or theatrical performers; those regulations weren't read, and the federal law exempts performers. Hours limits aren't held. Service: none. Guam's people are US citizens: Selective Service says almost all male US citizens and immigrants aged 18 through 25 must register (a duty not held here), and that it can't classify men for service when there is no active draft.
